claims.says: If a delta matrix represents a reference coordinate set, then after any operation sequence meeting its preconditions, with any fold decisions, it still represents the reference updated the same way.
Given sorted base, deletion and addition layers, the merge iterator with enough steps yields exactly the undeleted base entries merged in key order with the additions, an addition winning a tie.
Along any history of forks, writes, commits and abandons from a well-tracked state, no matrix handle referenced by an already published version ever changes its contents.
Adding a batch of distinct new edge ids to a node pair keeps every multi-edge storage invariant, and the pair's edges become exactly the old ones plus the batch.
Under the layer invariant, the deletion layer is no larger than the base, and nvals computed as base plus additions minus deletions equals the number of logical entries.
